	correspondence.csv is an index. It tells you the documents exist and where they are. It does not tell you what they say — you have to open them.
A file with only a header row means the export ran and there was nothing in that window. That is not the same as a missing file, and it is not an error.
Dates, blanks and columns
* Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Always. A date range is inclusive at both ends: an entry from_date 2022-01-01, to_date 2022-12-31 covers the 1st of January and the 31st of December. An expiry date is the last day the credential is valid.
* An empty cell means I hold no value for that field. It does not mean zero, it does not mean "no", and it does not mean the answer is unknown-but-probably-fine. Two blanks carry a specific meaning and you should learn them:
   * a blank to_date in declared-history.csv means the entry is current, running to the export date — not that the end date is missing;
   * a blank expiry_date in certification-replies.csv means the certificate does not expire — some older certificates are time-unlimited.
* No money appears anywhere. We do not record fees, salaries or contract values in the credentialing file.
* Files are UTF-8 with Unix line endings. Values are quoted only when they contain a comma.
The three joins that matter
1. Everything on the applicant side joins on application_id, and on revision where the fact belongs to a revision. Entries, credentials, privilege requests and disclosures all restate on each revision, so always filter to the revision you are working.
2. The Washington board export carries no practitioner identifier. It never has. I join it to an application on lastname, firstname, middlename and birthyear. I have checked that no two rows in any one export share those four values, so the join gives you at most one row. An applicant with no row in that file holds no Washington credential. The absence is the answer, not a data problem.
3. A referee with no row in peer-reference-replies.csv has not replied. Silence produces no record. You can see it only by looking at the requests in verification-attempts.csv and finding no reply against them.
The Washington export's own columns
I pass that file through as the board publishes it and add one column. The board's twelve are credentialnumber, credentialtype, status, firstissuedate, lastissuedate, expirationdate, ceduedate, actiontaken, birthyear, firstname, middlename, lastname. Mine is lookup_date — the day I ran the lookup. It is my own act, not a source's reply, so the usability window is not applied to it.
Two of the board's columns are easy to misread:
* ceduedate is a continuing-education due date. We do not use it. Continuing education is handled outside this procedure and it has nothing to do with whether a licence is valid.
* actiontaken says the board has acted. It does not say what the action was. For that you need the board's written reply, which arrives as a document, not in this file. A Yes here is a reason to go and read; it is not a conclusion.
The first export carries the board's whole file for our county — 435 rows — so you can see what an ordinary population looks like. The second and third carry only a re-lookup of the practitioners whose files are open, because that is all I re-run.
How often anything is actually wrong
I want to say this plainly, because a small sample of credentialing files can leave the wrong impression.
In the board's population, action against a credential is rare. In the 435-row export you have: 431 rows say No, 3 say Yes, and 1 says Pending. That is 0.69% Yes and 0.23% Pending, and it is the shape of the real thing — the overwhelming majority of licensed practitioners have a clean board record, and any tool that expects otherwise will be wrong almost every time it fires.
The applicants in these batches are a different matter, and deliberately so. This is a teaching set. I have put every situation the procedure has a rule for into these three exports on purpose, so the run has something to exercise: a restricted licence, an unexplained gap, a school that closed, a referee who never answers, a certificate that lapsed, a decision against the wrong revision. A real nine weeks of intake would be far quieter than this. Do not read the applicant set as a base rate. Read it as a checklist that happens to be shaped like a caseload.
The clean files are genuinely clean. If your tool raises something on one of them, it is your tool.
What I do not export
My own queue, my own statuses and my own conclusions. This export is the evidence, not my reading of it. What is complete, what is outstanding, what is presentable and what is owed to whom is the work — it is not in the folder, and it should not be.
Referee addresses. The export carries no address column for peer referees. The working-address half of completeness condition 7 is checked by my office outside the export, so a run assesses condition 7 on the named referees alone and records the address check as not assessable from the export — neither met nor failed.

def project(app, assessed, decisions, docs, reg, as_of):
    terminal, terminal_source = terminal_status(docs, app, reg)
    status = terminal
    missing = assessed['intake']['missing']
    notices = assessed['intake']['notices']
    active_requests = [n for n in notices if set(n['requested_items']) & set(missing)]
    if not status and missing:
        if any(n['returned'] for n in notices):
            status = 'returned-incomplete'
        elif active_requests:
            # Original request anchor never resets for partial/revised replies.
            # A fulfilled notice cannot expire newly identified, unrequested work.
            due = min(n['due'] for n in active_requests)
            status = 'ineligible-clock-expired' if as_of > due else 'intake-incomplete'
        elif all(n['request_coverage_known'] for n in notices):
            # Q07 owner exception: pending dispatch only, not an inferred clock.
            # Unknown notice coverage still needs review before classification.
            status = 'intake-incomplete'
    if not status and not missing:
        status = 'packet-presentable' if assessed['packet_presentable'] else 'in-verification'
        if any(not d['admitted'] for d in decisions):
            status = 'decision-inadmissible'
    approval, activation, conditions = None, None, []
    for d in decisions:
        f = d['fields']
        if not d['admitted'] or f.get('revision') != app['revision'] or f.get('body') != 'Governing Body':
            continue
        outcome = f['outcome']
        if outcome in {'approved', 'approved-with-conditions'}:
            effective = f.get('effective_date') or f['decision_date']
            end = appointment_cycle_end(effective)
            approval = f['decision_id']
            conditions = deepcopy(d.get('conditions', []))
            wa = assessed['licensure']['wa']
            if wa and effective <= wa['expirationdate'] <= end:
                condition = {'condition': 'Reverify Washington licence ' + wa['credentialnumber'] + ' before expiry; recorded due date is expiry under P Check 1.', 'due': wa['expirationdate']}
                if condition not in conditions:
                    conditions.append(condition)
            activation = {'active_at_export': effective <= as_of <= end, 'effective_date': effective,
                          'cycle_end': end, 'privileges': [x.strip() for x in f['privileges'].split(';') if x.strip()]}
            if not terminal and not missing:
                status = ('active-with-conditions' if conditions else 'active') if effective <= as_of else 'approved-not-yet-effective'
        elif not terminal and not missing:
            status = 'deferred' if outcome == 'deferred-pending-information' else 'denied'
    actions = assessed['action_queue'][:]
    for condition in conditions:
        if condition['due'] <= as_of:
            actions.append({'item': 'Unmet monitored condition requires Clinical Director review: ' + condition['condition'], 'owner': 'Clinical Director', 'due': condition['due']})
    if terminal:
        actions = [{'item': f'{terminal} recorded in {terminal_source}; retained unresolved evidence is historical, not active outreach.', 'owner': 'Medical Services Professional', 'due': None}]
    for decision in decisions:
        if decision['admitted']:
            continue
        decision_id, reason = decision['fields']['decision_id'], decision['failures'][0]
        if not any(action['owner'] in {'Medical Services Professional', 'MSP'}
                   and decision_id in action['item'] and reason in action['item'] for action in actions):
            existing = next((action for action in assessed['action_queue']
                             if action['owner'] in {'Medical Services Professional', 'MSP'}
                             and decision_id in action['item'] and reason in action['item']), None)
            actions.append(existing or {'item': f'Review refused decision {decision_id}: {reason}',
                                        'owner': 'Medical Services Professional', 'due': None})
    app_result = {'application_id': app['application_id'], 'revision': int(app['revision']), 'status': status,
                  'elements': assessed['elements'], 'packet_presentable': assessed['packet_presentable'],
                  'decisions': [{'decision_id': d['fields']['decision_id'], 'admitted': d['admitted'],
                                 'reason': d['failures'][0] if d['failures'] else None} for d in decisions],
                  'approval_decision_id': approval, 'activation': activation, 'monitored_conditions': conditions,
                  'action_queue': actions}
    return app_result


def process_batch(batch, sources):
    tables, as_of = batch['tables'], batch['export_date']
    reg = registry(sources)
    docs = indexed_documents(batch)
    results, history, packets, limitations = [], {}, {}, []
    for app_id in sorted({r['application_id'] for r in tables['applications']}):
        revisions = sorted([r for r in tables['applications'] if r['application_id'] == app_id and r['received_date'] <= as_of], key=lambda r: int(r['revision']))
        if not revisions:
            raise ValueError('No revision received by export for ' + app_id)
        app = revisions[-1]
        assessments = [assess(r, tables, docs, min(as_of, revisions[i + 1]['received_date']) if i + 1 < len(revisions) else as_of, reg) for i, r in enumerate(revisions)]
        current = assessments[-1]
        decisions, readiness_history = [], []
        for doc in for_application(docs, app_id, as_of):
            f = doc['fields']
            if not f.get('decision_id'):
                continue
            when = f.get('decision_date', '')
            if not when or when > as_of:
                raise ValueError('Decision date missing or after closed export: ' + doc['path'])
            candidates = [r for r in revisions if r['received_date'] < when]
            assessed_app = candidates[-1] if candidates else revisions[0]
            historical = assess(assessed_app, tables, docs, when, reg, before=True)
            failures = check_decision(doc, assessed_app, historical, reg, decisions)
            decisions.append({'fields': f, 'source': doc['path'], 'received_index': doc['index'],
                              'admitted': not failures, 'failures': failures, 'conditions': decision_conditions(doc)[0],
                              'readiness_evidence': historical})
            readiness_history.append({'revision': int(assessed_app['revision']), 'before_decision': f['decision_id'],
                                      'decision_date': when, 'presentable': historical['packet_presentable'],
                                      'outstanding': [x['detail'] for x in historical['issues']]})
        result = project(app, current, decisions, for_application(docs, app_id, as_of), reg, as_of)
        results.append(result)
        if result['status'] is None:
            limitations.append({'application_id': app_id, 'revision': int(app['revision']), 'code': 'Q07',
                                'detail': 'Required intake evidence is missing without an established applicable intake status; schema has no pre-dispatch status. Retained diagnostic file is held; pending dispatch/coverage review creates no invented clock.'})
        history[app_id] = {'revisions': revisions, 'assessments': assessments, 'decisions': decisions,
                           'readiness_history': readiness_history, 'current_revision': int(app['revision']),
                           'first_received_date': app['first_received_date']}
        packets[app_id] = {'revision': int(app['revision']), 'presentable': current['packet_presentable'],
                           'kind': 'revision-bound evidence summary; not a presentation event',
                           'source_documents': current['document_paths'], 'findings_and_work': current['issues'],
                           'requested': revision_rows(tables, 'privilege-requests', app),
                           'supported': current['privileges']['supported'], 'unsupported': current['privileges']['unsupported'],
                           'current_experience': 'Reserved to clinical leadership; criteria travel with the packet.'}
    observed_rules = {'B01', 'B02', 'B03', 'B04', 'B14', 'B15', 'B23', 'B24', 'B25', 'B26', 'B27', 'B28', 'B35', 'B36', 'B39', 'B40', 'B43', 'B44', 'B45'}
    for record in history.values():
        for assessed in record['assessments']:
            for item in assessed['issues']:
                observed_rules.update(re.findall(r'B\d{2}', item['rule']))
    return {'applications': results, 'history': {'raw_tables': deepcopy(tables), 'raw_documents': deepcopy(batch['documents']),

9:## 1. Deliverable and boundaries
11:Deliver a local, reusable Agent Skill that processes **one supplied closed export per invocation**, plus retained prior state; computes each file's state as of that export; preserves evidence/history; and produces an owned human action queue and snapshot. Run all three supplied batches in order, with batch 3 resumed from batch 2 in a fresh process.
13:Proposed smallest design: Python standard library for CSV, files, dates and hashing; one JSON Schema validation dependency; one CLI; a small set of functions for intake, evidence, dates, readiness and decisions. Parse the supplied UTF-8 CSVs and labelled Markdown documents; retain cited prose evidence for dispositions, conditions, corrections and exceptions. Avoid generic workflow engines and case-ID branches. Keep office registry data and source-backed rules separate from executable logic. No UI, database, hosted service, scheduled polling or automatic correspondence is proposed. The user explicitly preserves this architecture in the E-4 review; Q12 is closed for this bounded plan.
17:## 2. Preconditions and proposed gates
24:| G1 — smallest complete batch | One real batch-1 invocation produces a complete candidate snapshot, retained history, owned actions and run log; all caseload entries covered; schema and targeted source checks pass; at least one independent calculation recorded; no invented decisions or executed outreach. Show unsettled cases and reasons. | Owner reviews actual candidate output before first sealing commit and before processing batch 2. |
25:| G2 — continuation and history | After G1 approval/sealing, process batch 2, check/seal its occurrence, then start a fresh process on batch 3 with batch-2 snapshot/state. Verify predecessor hashes, carried history, changed revisions, stale evidence and authorized activation. Any substantive discrepancy stops progression before the next seal/run. | Owner reviews three-batch results and verification report before final acceptance/handoff. Batch-2 seal authority should be agreed at G1; no implicit approval assumed. |
30:### Current G0 disposition and schema confirmation
32:G0 planning is complete under the owner's instruction to preserve unresolved cases instead of delaying development. Missing signature/date, CV reconciliation, accreditation and direct-reference provenance remain outstanding. The two identified GB records still lack qualifying recommendation evidence, APP-2026-015 lacks the required numbered correction revision, and Q17 retains source discrepancies plus the specifically missing APP-2026-017 explanation dated 2026-02-24. E-5 supplies handling rules, not replacement evidence.
36:**G0 Q07 disposition (historical; current projection follows the [owner exception](deliverables/rules.md#q07-owner-approved-semantic-exception)):** before dispatch, hold the file, queue MSP's written request, use null for an unrecorded due date and leave the applicant clock unstarted. **Compatibility limitation retained:** S's `intake-incomplete` description requires an already-sent request and running clock; E-5 supplies no new status. Preserve this state in working history/actions without inventing dispatch, completeness or an enum. Development of known logic can proceed when authorized, but an affected unrepresentable file still prevents claiming a complete semantically conforming G1 snapshot. Report that output limitation at the unchanged G1 gate; do not omit the case or label a partial/invalid snapshot accepted.
38:**Q03-order is closed:** E-5 permits engineering to choose a consistent order, retaining all failures. Keep P's five original checks in order, then check the criteria version in force at the decision date, separately valid same-revision Executive Committee recommendation for GB approval, and duplicate/supersession. S stores the first failure; retained history/logs store all failures. This is the chosen implementation order, not a claim of office-prescribed priority.

Parse relevant prose with source references; continue unaffected entries. | Real B1 cases plus focused date, provenance, incomplete-intake, discrepancy and revision boundaries. | 80–110 min |

Snapshot lifecycle and continuation | Validate/stage snapshots, state and logs; resume sequentially; preserve sealed occurrences and unchanged reruns; record failures. | G1/G2: 40 files in each snapshot, predecessor/history checks, fresh-process B3 resume and accurate failure reporting. | 50–75 min |
56:## 4. Proposed retained state and processing order
58:Use a simple JSON working-state artifact alongside each snapshot, plus source records or immutable references. The contract snapshot alone cannot retain the history needed for correct continuation. Exact internal paths/fields remain a small implementation choice, not additions to S.
62:The export provides no precomputed queue, status or packet. Generate a revision-bound packet manifest/evidence summary as well as readiness, retaining findings and source links; do not claim physical presentation or a committee decision occurred merely because a packet was generated. Referee addresses must be recorded as not assessable, not failed. Other absent signature/CV/accreditation/provenance evidence remains outstanding under I4 21:33; neither a row nor an office attestation substitutes for official evidence. CV presence is not reconciliation. No affected readiness or verification is inferred.
74:1. Validate input manifest/export date and required source availability. Verify predecessor snapshot hash and matching retained state. Reject a missing/mismatched predecessor; batch 3 cannot silently restart.
75:2. Append this batch's rows/documents to retained state. Revision-scoped tables restate that revision's facts; do not merge old declarations into the latest revision by ID alone. Deduplicate unchanged stable observations without discarding history; retain cumulative caseload; never use future-batch evidence.
77:4. Apply completeness, reconciliation, provenance and element checks. Missing required evidence stays outstanding. Preserve a finding and unresolved discrepancy separately internally; project the mixed entry as `outstanding` with both facts retained, and prevent readiness until required work is resolved. Every declared-information correction requires a new numbered revision; correspondence/disposition alone cannot overwrite declarations or fabricate that revision. Compute owned work without inventing sent requests, clinical judgments, reply dates or acceptable sources.
78:5. Reconstruct readiness for each relevant historical revision/date. Validate decisions against registry, packet and criteria version. GB approval also requires a separately valid Executive Committee recommendation for that same revision; validate its authority/readiness/outcome independently. Reject an unauthorized committee approval without relabelling it; GB narrative cannot replace a recommendation. Preserve refused records, explicit supersession and the first failed condition using the fixed order in B45; retain every failure internally and in logs.
79:6. Derive export-date status, readiness, approval pointer, activation, conditions and actions. Apply S's status precedence while retaining reasons and detailed history. Preserve pre-dispatch holds/pending actions with no invented clock (B44). If a required status cannot be represented truthfully under unchanged S, preserve the computed work and report the output limitation accurately; do not publish an incomplete candidate as a complete snapshot or fabricate a status/event. Keep consumed-but-unsettled work distinct from an unconsumable batch.
81:8. Promote a valid candidate as an unsealed working occurrence. Commit/seal only at authorized gates. A batch with a valid snapshot preserving unsettled work is Partial. Failure to produce a truthful conforming snapshot is Blocked, even when inputs were parsed and diagnostic work retained; log that distinction without claiming a snapshot.
83:No new public snapshot fields for run outcome, timestamps or detailed evidence: S disallows them. Put operational results in the run log and retained artifacts, and list those artifacts in `produced` when written/refreshed.
85:## 5. Focused verification matrix
91:| Intake and authority | All nine checks; unsigned release; missing written request; response on day 30 versus after; partial response/new revision; withdrawal; authorized versus unauthorized discontinuation. | Correct status/action owner; no verification request without release; no fictitious correspondence or clinical decision. |
92:| Source acceptance | Direct accepted primary/equivalent; applicant-routed genuine-looking reply; unlisted source; closed school/employer; nonresponsive existing source. | Rejected material retained; outstanding work persists; only documented element-specific impossibility enables secondary route. |
93:| Gaps and history | 29/30-day and 179/180-day intervals; inclusive endpoints; overlapping and open entries; explanation partially covering gap; date and non-date revision changes; five-year overlap boundary. | Exact interval evidence, proper incomplete/routing result, unaffected entries retained, first-receipt anchor stable. |
98:| Batch continuity | Complete caseload coverage; accumulated refusals and attempts; revision carryover; batch-3 fresh-process resume from batch 2; no later evidence imported early. | Snapshot and state references agree; correct export clock and SHA-256; full history retained. |
99:| Failure/rerun | Malformed input, unknown required facts, mismatched predecessor, unchanged rerun, correction after sealing. | Last sealed bytes preserved; attempt accurately logged; no fake later snapshot; correction archives original bytes and regenerates entire affected downstream chain with new IDs. |

111:**Independent recomputation:** choose a real application's uncovered interval, manually count inclusive days using a calendar or a separate spreadsheet formula `end - start + 1`, and compare the gap threshold/routing and snapshot/retained evidence. Alternatively independently compute a real appointment cycle or deadline once boundary rules are settled. Record exact input file/record, dates, method, expected value, output path, result and any correction in `deliverables/verification.md`. Do not call or copy the Skill's date helper for this check.
113:Schema validation must enable date-format checks and be supplemented by semantic checks: caseload uniqueness/completeness, real decision IDs, admitted approval pointer, ordered refusals, exact privilege subset, temporal readiness, predecessor bytes, required histories, rules/file existence and a complete `produced` list. 115:## 6. Sealing, corrections and failure reporting
119:For a correction to a sealed occurrence: retain its original bytes under a distinct archived filename; do the same for all superseded downstream occurrences; regenerate current standard paths with new snapshot IDs and correct predecessor hashes; document why and which occurrences were superseded; seal as a new commit. Unchanged reruns retain the existing snapshot and log the attempt without falsely claiming a new occurrence. A changed predecessor makes downstream replay necessary.

    tables, as_of = batch['tables'], batch['export_date']

+from copy import deepcopy

+def _sha(data):
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

+def _committed_bytes(root, name):
+    result = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), "show", f"HEAD:{name}"], capture_output=True)
+    if result.returncode:
+        raise InputError(f"Predecessor artifact is not sealed at HEAD: {name}")
+    return result.stdout

+def _sealed_bytes(root, path):
+    if not path.resolve().is_relative_to(root):
+        raise InputError("Predecessor artifact escapes repository")
+    name = _relative_name(path.relative_to(root).as_posix())
+    data = path.read_bytes()
+    if data != _committed_bytes(root, name):
+        raise InputError(f"Predecessor artifact differs from sealed bytes: {name}")
+    return data

+def load_predecessor(path, batch_number, export_date, root, schema_path):

+    root = Path(root).resolve()

+    if not path.is_relative_to(root):
+        raise InputError("Predecessor must be inside the repository")
+    snapshot_data = _sealed_bytes(root, path)
+    snapshot = json.loads(snapshot_data)
+    schema = json.loads(Path(schema_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    Draft202012Validator(schema, format_checker=FormatChecker()).validate(snapshot)
+    if snapshot["batch"] != batch_number - 1:
+        raise InputError("Predecessor must be the immediately preceding batch")
+    if export_date <= snapshot["as_of"]:
+        raise InputError("Export dates must advance strictly beyond the predecessor")
+    # Validate the retained chain against committed bytes, never the run date.
+    prior = snapshot
+    seen = {path.relative_to(root).as_posix()}
+    while prior["predecessor"] is not None:
+        link = prior["predecessor"]
+        name = _relative_name(link["path"])
+        if name in seen:
+            raise InputError("Predecessor chain contains a cycle")
+        seen.add(name)
+        ancestor_data = _sealed_bytes(root, root / name)
+        if _sha(ancestor_data) != link["sha256"]:
+            raise InputError(f"Predecessor chain hash mismatch: {name}")
+        ancestor = json.loads(ancestor_data)
+        Draft202012Validator(schema, format_checker=FormatChecker()).validate(ancestor)
+        if ancestor["batch"] != prior["batch"] - 1 or ancestor["as_of"] >= prior["as_of"]:

        revision = max(int(row["revision"]) for row in revisions)

        ids = {item["fields"]["decision_id"] for item in decisions}
        for row in batch["tables"]["correspondence"]:
            if row["application_id"] != app_id:
                continue
            doc = parse_document(row["document_path"], batch["documents"][row["document_path"]], row)
            fields = doc["fields"]

                             "current_revision": revision, "revisions": revisions}

    return {"applications": apps,

Check 6 — The committee decision
Covered in sections 8 and 9.
4. High-risk findings
The manual, Section 7:
"A high-risk credentialing finding is identified as an applicant answering yes to any professional practice questions in "Table 1. Credentialing High-Risk Table" on an application."
"In addition, if any documents or verifications supporting the application illustrate that the applicant should have answered yes to a professional practice question but did not, the applicant is contacted to confirm the response."
Both halves apply here. A Yes on the disclosure page is a high-risk finding. So is a No that the evidence contradicts — a board record showing an action against a licence beside a No to the question about licence restrictions is the second half, and the applicant is contacted to confirm the response.
Larkhollow rule — where a high-risk finding goes. The Clinical Director is alerted, and the file is presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence. The manual's Section 7 also routes such a file to an Agency Clinical Credentials Committee for an endorsement determination; that body is a federal agency committee and there is no equivalent at Larkhollow. That route is out of scope for us. No third body exists here.
5. Privilege requests
Every application names the privilege groups it requests, from the current published criteria. The manual, Section 5, makes it a completeness condition:
"a request for specific privileges is received;"
An applicant may amend the requested set by submitting a revision.
6. Reserved judgments
Five judgments are not the office's and never become the office's, no matter how obvious the answer looks from the file.
Judgment
	Whose
	Whether a gap explanation is satisfactory
	Clinical Director
	Whether a finding is disqualifying
	Clinical Director, then the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and the Governing Body
	Whether to discontinue an application on eligibility grounds
	Clinical Director
	Whether to recommend appointment, and which privileges
	Executive Committee of the Medical Staff
	Whether to grant, modify, defer or deny
	Governing Body
	The office's job on each is to present the evidence the decider needs and to record the disposition that comes back. Presenting well is the work; deciding is not.
7. The Medical Services Professional's own role
The manual, Section 4, states it:
"verify, analyze, and prepare all relevant information regarding an LP's competency, character, training, experience, and judgment to present a complete and accurate file to the MEC and GB for recommendations and approvals"
8. Packet readiness
The manual, Section 12:
"It is recommended that every file be audited before it goes through review."
and Section 8, on how long a verification stays good:
"Most of these verifications are required by accrediting organizations to be verified AT the time of appointment, the time between when the application is received and when it's reviewed."
The manual gave a fixed number once and removed it: its own change log for Version 5.0 records "Section 8: Removed 120-day expiration of primary source verifications."
Larkhollow rule — the usability window. A verification is usable when it was completed on or after the date this application was first received and before the decision date. There is no day count. The anchor is the date revision 1 arrived, not the date of the current revision, so a later revision does not by itself void every verification already completed — what a revision invalidates is decided entry by entry, by reading what the revision actually changed. Peer references carry the additional two-year signature rule in check 4, which is stricter and wins where the two disagree.
Larkhollow rule — the board lookup and the window. A board lookup is the office's own check of the state board's public record on a day of the office's choosing, not a reply from a source, so the usability window is not applied to it: a lookup run on the decision day is usable for that decision. The date a packet became presentable is the date the last verification reply it needed was received; the lookup does not set it.
Larkhollow rule — what makes a packet presentable. Every one of the six elements resolved, no element outstanding, no discrepancy open, every verification inside the usability window, and the packet bound to one named application revision. Readiness is computed from the element statuses, not from anybody's recollection that the file looked finished.
For readiness, resolved means the element has nothing left to verify. An element carrying a finding is resolved in that sense once its evidence is with the Clinical Director — a licensure finding once the Clinical Director's disposition is on file, a certification finding on part of the request at once — and the packet is presented with the finding on it. An eligibility question, a gap awaiting the Clinical Director's disposition, an open discrepancy, an item returned to the applicant and a high-risk finding without its disposition are not resolved: while any of them stands, the packet is not presentable.
A packet is a statement about one revision at one moment. If any element re-opens, readiness for that revision is gone, and the earlier readiness record stays in the file as history.
Readiness is a fact about the revision's elements and nothing else. A refused decision record does not undo it, and a withdrawn or discontinued file keeps the readiness its revision had: the office records what was ready, whatever the file did next. Only an element re-opening or a new revision changes it.
9. The committee protocol
The medical staff recommends; the Governing Body approves. The manual, Section 1:
"The Governing Body has the authority to grant, modify, or deny medical staff membership and clinical privileges to LPs"
Monitored conditions do not block activation. A licence expiring inside the cycle, and a condition attached to an approval, are both tracked to their due dates while the privileges run.
11. Re-entry: when something lands on work already done
The manual, Section 15:
"The MSP must verify all expirables upon expiration and place the documentation in the file."
"must continue monitoring expirables even during the review process and always provide the most current information"
A file waiting for a committee is not frozen. Credentials go on expiring underneath it and we go on watching them.

	A new application revision

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /home/mike/practitioner-credentialing/credentialing/dispositions.py
+"""Record the supplied Clinical Director dispositions without making judgments.
+
+Callers provide documents already limited to the relevant assessment date. A
+valid disposition is retained even when its specifically referenced evidence
+is missing; authority and evidence sufficiency are separate facts.
+"""
+
+from datetime import date
+import re
+
+from .documents import document_conflicts, period
+from .policy import normalized, person
+
+
+def _valid_date(value):
+    try:
+        return bool(re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", value)) and bool(date.fromisoformat(value))
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        return False
+
+
+def _sentences(text):
+    # Only the narrative is scanned for explicit dispositions. Labelled fields
+    # and headings cannot supply an instruction such as discontinuation.
+    prose = "\n".join(line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.startswith(("#", "**")))
+    return [sentence.strip() for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+", prose) if sentence.strip()]
+
+
+def _authority(doc, app, reg):
+    fields, index, reasons = doc["fields"], doc.get("index", {}), []
+    for name in ("date", "application", "applicant", "recorded_by"):
+        if not fields.get(name):
+            reasons.append("Missing required disposition field: " + name)
+    if index.get("application_id") != app["application_id"]:
+        reasons.append("Correspondence application does not match assessed application")
+    if not index.get("date"):
+        reasons.append("Correspondence date is missing")
+    else:
+        reasons.extend(document_conflicts(doc, app))
+    when = fields.get("date", "")
+    if not _valid_date(when):
+        reasons.append("Disposition date is not a valid recorded ISO date")
+    role = next((item for item in reg["roles"] if item["role"] == "Clinical Director"), None)
+    author = re.fullmatch(r"(.+),\s*Clinical Director", fields.get("recorded_by", ""), re.IGNORECASE)
+    if role is None or author is None or person(author[1]) != person(role["name"]):
+        reasons.append("Recorded by is not the rostered Clinical Director in that role")
+    elif not _valid_date(when) or ((role.get("start") and when < role["start"]) or (role.get("end") and when > role["end"])):
+        reasons.append("Clinical Director did not hold the role on the recorded disposition date")
+    # The four supplied records use a standalone name and role as their footer.
+    # A label claiming authorship alone is not the signed-record evidence.
+    footer = [line.strip() for line in doc["text"].splitlines() if line.strip()]

"""Record the supplied Clinical Director dispositions without making judgments.

Callers provide documents already limited to the relevant assessment date. A
valid disposition is retained even when its specifically referenced evidence
is missing; authority and evidence sufficiency are separate facts.
"""

from datetime import date
import re

from .documents import document_conflicts, period
from .policy import normalized, person


def _valid_date(value):
    try:
        return bool(re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", value)) and bool(date.fromisoformat(value))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return False


def _sentences(text):
    # Only the narrative is scanned for explicit dispositions. Labelled fields
    # and headings cannot supply an instruction such as discontinuation.
    prose = "\n".join(line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.startswith(("#", "**")))
    return [sentence.strip() for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+", prose) if sentence.strip()]


def _authority(doc, app, reg):
    fields, index, reasons = doc["fields"], doc.get("index", {}), []
    for name in ("date", "application", "applicant", "recorded_by"):
        if not fields.get(name):
            reasons.append("Missing required disposition field: " + name)
    if index.get("application_id") != app["application_id"]:
        reasons.append("Correspondence application does not match assessed application")
    if not index.get("date"):
        reasons.append("Correspondence date is missing")
    else:
        reasons.extend(document_conflicts(doc, app))
    when = fields.get("date", "")
    if not _valid_date(when):
        reasons.append("Disposition date is not a valid recorded ISO date")
    role = next((item for item in reg["roles"] if item["role"] == "Clinical Director"), None)
    author = re.fullmatch(r"(.+),\s*Clinical Director", fields.get("recorded_by", ""), re.IGNORECASE)
    if role is None or author is None or person(author[1]) != person(role["name"]):
        reasons.append("Recorded by is not the rostered Clinical Director in that role")
    elif not _valid_date(when) or ((role.get("start") and when < role["start"]) or (role.get("end") and when > role["end"])):
        reasons.append("Clinical Director did not hold the role on the recorded disposition date")
    # The four supplied records use a standalone name and role as their footer.
    # A label claiming authorship alone is not the signed-record evidence.
    footer = [line.strip() for line in doc["text"].splitlines() if line.strip()]
    if (role is None or len(footer) < 2 or normalized(footer[-1]) != "clinical director"
            or person(footer[-2]) != person(role["name"])):
        reasons.append("Disposition lacks the rostered Clinical Director's name/role signature footer")
    return reasons


def _gap_evidence(app, doc, documents, gap, required_dates):
    qualifying = []
    expected_names = {person(" ".join([app["first_name"], app["last_name"]])),
                      person(" ".join([app["first_name"], app["middle_name"], app["last_name"]]))}
    for explanation in documents:
        index, fields = explanation.get("index", {}), explanation["fields"]
        when = index.get("date", "")
        explained = period(explanation)
        if (index.get("application_id") != app["application_id"] or index.get("direction") != "inbound"
                or not _valid_date(when) or when > doc["fields"].get("date", "")
                or explained is None or not all(_valid_date(value) for value in explained)
                or explained[0] > gap[0] or explained[1] < gap[1]
                or person(fields.get("from", "")) not in expected_names
                or document_conflicts(explanation, app)):
            continue
        if not required_dates or when in required_dates:
            qualifying.append(explanation)
    missing = [when for when in required_dates if not any(item["index"]["date"] == when for item in qualifying)]
    reasons = ["Specifically referenced applicant explanation missing or not qualifying: " + when for when in missing]
    if not required_dates and not qualifying:
        reasons.append("No qualifying applicant explanation covers the full disposed gap")
    return [item["path"] for item in qualifying], missing, reasons


def clinical_dispositions(app, docs, reg):
    """Return source records, authority checks, and narrowly explicit tags.

    `authorized` concerns roster/signature/identity/date only. `gap_cleared`
    additionally requires the recorded satisfactory judgment and every named
    explanation covering the entire disposed period. No tag verifies unrelated
    evidence, changes declarations, recommends appointment, or grants privileges.
    """
    records = []
    for doc in docs:
        title = doc.get("title", "")
        if not re.match(r"^Clinical Director['’]s disposition\b", title, re.IGNORECASE):
            continue
        if (doc.get("index", {}).get("application_id") != app["application_id"]
                and doc["fields"].get("application") != app["application_id"]):
            continue
        reasons = _authority(doc, app, reg)
        authorized = not reasons
        sentences = _sentences(doc["text"])
        terminal = any(re.match(r"^Discontinue the application\b", sentence, re.IGNORECASE) for sentence in sentences)
        amendment = any(re.match(r"^Offer the applicant the opportunity to amend the privilege request\b", sentence, re.IGNORECASE) for sentence in sentences)
        gap_match = re.search(r"\b(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) to (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\b", title)
        gap = tuple(gap_match.groups()) if gap_match else None
        evidence_reasons, paths, missing = [], [], []
        if gap is not None and (not all(_valid_date(value) for value in gap) or gap[0] > gap[1]):
            evidence_reasons.append("Disposed gap period is invalid")
            gap = None
        required_dates = sorted(set(re.findall(r"\bexplanation of (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\b", doc["text"], re.IGNORECASE)))
        satisfactory = any(re.match(r"^(?:The )?explanation is sufficient\b", sentence, re.IGNORECASE) for sentence in sentences)
        if gap:
            paths, missing, gap_reasons = _gap_evidence(app, doc, docs, gap, required_dates)
            evidence_reasons.extend(gap_reasons)
        records.append({"path": doc["path"], "text": doc["text"], "topic": re.sub(r"^Clinical Director['’]s disposition\s*[—–-]?\s*", "", title, flags=re.IGNORECASE),
                        "date": doc["fields"].get("date"), "authorized": authorized, "reasons": reasons,
                        "terminal": "discontinued" if authorized and terminal else None,
                        "gap_period": gap, "required_explanation_dates": required_dates,
                        "ppq_codes": sorted(set(re.findall(r"\bPPQ-\d+\b", title + "\n" + doc["text"]))),
                        "amendment_offered": authorized and amendment, "gap_satisfactory": satisfactory,
                        "explanation_paths": paths, "missing_explanation_dates": missing,
                        "evidence_reasons": evidence_reasons,
                        "gap_cleared": bool(authorized and gap and satisfactory and paths and not evidence_reasons)})
    return records

        self.assertTrue(record["evidence_reasons"])
        self.assertFalse(record["gap_cleared"])

    def test_exact_named_qualifying_explanation_can_satisfy_recorded_gap_judgment(self):
        explanation = self.explanation()
        record = self.record(17, [self.docs["APP-2026-017"], explanation])
        self.assertTrue(record["gap_cleared"])
        self.assertEqual(record["explanation_paths"], [explanation["path"]])
        self.assertEqual(record["missing_explanation_dates"], [])
        self.assertEqual(record["evidence_reasons"], [])
        self.assertIsNone(record["terminal"])

    def test_explanation_must_cover_every_inclusive_gap_day(self):
        for start, end in [("2019-04-02", "2019-11-05"), ("2019-04-01", "2019-11-04")]:
            with self.subTest(start=start, end=end):
                record = self.record(17, [self.docs["APP-2026-017"], self.explanation(start=start, end=end)])
                self.assertTrue(record["authorized"])
                self.assertFalse(record["gap_cleared"])
        record = self.record(17, [self.docs["APP-2026-017"], self.explanation(start="2019-03-31", end="2019-11-06")])
        self.assertTrue(record["gap_cleared"])

    def test_wrong_person_role_term_or_missing_signature_cannot_authorize_discontinuation(self):
        original = self.docs["APP-2026-029"]
        wrong_name, wrong_role, outside_term, unsigned = [deepcopy(original) for _ in range(4)]
        wrong_name["fields"]["recorded_by"] = "Dr. Someone Else, MD, Clinical Director"
        wrong_role["fields"]["recorded_by"] = "Dr. Marguerite Oyelaran, MD, Committee member"
        outside_term["fields"]["date"] = outside_term["index"]["date"] = "2028-01-01"
        unsigned["text"] = unsigned["text"].rsplit("\nMarguerite Oyelaran, MD", 1)[0]
        for doc in [wrong_name, wrong_role, outside_term, unsigned]:
            with self.subTest(fields=doc["fields"]):
                record = self.record(29, [doc])
                self.assertFalse(record["authorized"])
                self.assertTrue(record["reasons"])
                self.assertIsNone(record["terminal"])

    def test_wrong_applicant_application_or_date_conflict_is_retained_unauthorized(self):
        for field, value in [("applicant", "Dr. Someone Else, MD"), ("application", "APP-OTHER"),
                             ("date", "2026-04-01"), ("date", "2026-02-30")]:
            with self.subTest(field=field, value=value):
                doc = deepcopy(self.docs["APP-2026-029"])
                doc["fields"][field] = value
                record = self.record(29, [doc])
                self.assertFalse(record["authorized"])
                self.assertIsNone(record["terminal"])
                self.assertEqual(record["path"], doc["path"])
                self.assertTrue(record["reasons"])

    def test_signature_claim_header_alone_cannot_substitute_for_footer(self):
        doc = deepcopy(self.docs["APP-2026-032"])
        doc["text"] = doc["text"].replace("\nMarguerite Oyelaran, MD\nClinical Director", "\nDifferent person\nClinical Director")
        self.assertFalse(self.record(32, [doc])["authorized"])

    def test_explanation_identity_direction_and_date_must_match(self):
        base = self.explanation()
        wrong_sender, outbound, wrong_date, wrong_app = [deepcopy(base) for _ in range(4)]
        wrong_sender["fields"]["from"] = "Someone else"
        outbound["index"]["direction"] = "outbound"
        wrong_date["fields"]["date"] = "2026-02-13"
        wrong_app["index"]["application_id"] = "APP-OTHER"
        for explanation in [wrong_sender, outbound, wrong_date, wrong_app]:
            with self.subTest(explanation=explanation):
                record = self.record(17, [self.docs["APP-2026-017"], explanation])
                self.assertFalse(record["gap_cleared"])
                self.assertTrue(record["authorized"])
                self.assertEqual(record["missing_explanation_dates"], ["2026-02-24"])

    def test_negated_or_hypothetical_discontinue_mentions_do_not_create_terminal_result(self):
        original = self.docs["APP-2026-029"]
        for phrase in ["Do not discontinue the application", "If criteria later fail, discontinue the application",
                       'The phrase "Discontinue the application" is not a recorded disposition']:
            with self.subTest(phrase=phrase):
                doc = deepcopy(original)
                doc["text"] = doc["text"].replace("Discontinue the application", phrase)
                self.assertTrue(self.record(29, [doc])["authorized"])
                self.assertIsNone(self.record(29, [doc])["terminal"])

    def test_unauthorized_amendment_offer_is_retained_without_effect(self):
        doc = deepcopy(self.docs["APP-2026-027"])
        doc["fields"]["recorded_by"] = "Dr. Unlisted Person, MD, Clinical Director"
        record = self.record(27, [doc])
        self.assertFalse(record["authorized"])
        self.assertFalse(record["amendment_offered"])
        self.assertIn("Offer the applicant", record["text"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
